_Entry 0342_  
  
The vizier is finally dead. That...saga has ended, and dawn has broken once again. There was a day where Isgarren thought to get involved in these global affairs once Legavo (the "Scepter of Orr") resurfaced, but the ward's numbers are still weak following Eparch's last push during the Century of Darkness. Hundreds of years, and we're still climbing out of that hole.  
   
For a long while, Isgarren suspected that Eparch was the one toying with the vizier's mind; for that reason, we remained close to the situation. Wayfinder Aziure became our eyes after the Searing forced us to move the Beacon of Ages to the north, where I write now. Aziure and the Order—led now by Sir Ardaric—have been our most frequent of allies, crossing paths pre- and post-Cataclysm. Our connections are largely severed today, despite their aid in keeping more...nefarious parties from the gates of the Wizard's Tower. Another chapter closed.     
  
Through our investigations we learned of Abaddon's manipulations; it wasn't Eparch who brought Nightfall upon Tyria, but one of them. [lbracket]REDACTED[rbracket] We aren't to get involved with any quandary of the "gods." [lbracket]REDACTED[rbracket] I am informed that these notations may be pulled at a later date.  
  
Following our own recovery efforts after the battle of [lbracket]REDACTED[rbracket], Mabon is headed to Janthir. We imagine that the mursaat are dwindling, and with a handful of titans still remaining on this side of the veil. He intends to establish a warding enchantment, though the reasoning for such has been limited to the court. The newly established Rift Hunters will also be using their reprieve from Astral Ward duties to venture into the Tyrian mainland in search of lingering Mistborn threats.      
  
End of record.

*The Heart of the Obscure hums in your possession. Your eyes flash, and the old mursaat script on the scroll shifts until it becomes familiar—readable.*  
  
I have come here many times at Darda's suggestion to break away, to reflect, to mourn. Thoughts of my kin have soured as of late. The youngest among our gilded—Manikaz, Poloni, Seraf, Baraq—they are lost. They claw and scrape at the talons of their idols, dripping with zealotry, and for what? Optimus, Lazarus, Sarlic, and the rest are gambling with our people's future, terrified by the visions of some outcast scion.  
  
Some few of us elders keep to the fringes. For some of us, the isolation...the freedom from the prying eyes of the seers—paid in blood—was reward enough. To risk exposure and wage war against the peoples of this age is...to court our extinction.   
  
***  
  
The worst has come to pass. The titans have laid siege to the city; our people's corpses litter its halls. Darda and I, we... I do not know if anyone else made it out, but we will not linger, even for other survivors. She suggests we cross the ocean to the west of the horn and put this land behind us.  
  
I wanted to write on this scroll, to see this view once more before we fade from mortal memory and time. The storms rolling in over the lowlands to the south are beautiful this time of year. The bearkin will be on the move soon, I imagine. I will never see them dance again, hidden though I was.  
  
Janthir, I bid you farewell,  
Orestes, Archivist Exultant
